content.prompt:
Perform the following divisions and express each result in this form
$$\frac{P(x)}{D(x)}=Q(x)+\frac{R(x)}{D(x)}$$

answer.worked:
Divide the leading terms at each stage: $x^2\div x=x$, then $-5x\div x=-5$.
$$\begin{aligned}
(x^2-4x+1)-(x^2+x)&=-5x+1\\
(-5x+1)-(-5x-5)&=6\\
Q(x)&=x-5\\
R(x)&=6\\
\frac{x^2-4x+1}{x+1}&=x-5+\frac{6}{x+1}
\end{aligned}$$

Divide the leading terms at each stage: $x^2\div x=x$, then $-x\div x=-1$.
$$\begin{aligned}
(x^2-6x+5)-(x^2-5x)&=-x+5\\
(-x+5)-(-x+5)&=0\\
Q(x)&=x-1\\
R(x)&=0\\
\frac{x^2-6x+5}{x-5}&=x-1
\end{aligned}$$

content.prompt:
Consider the example $(4x^3+x-550)\div(x-5)$.

This polynomial is missing the $x^2$ term. When there are “gaps” in a polynomial, it is useful to insert any missing terms using a coefficient of $0$ so you can keep the terms lined up.

answer.worked:
Insert the missing term $0x^2$. Divide the leading terms, multiply by $x-5$ and subtract at each stage.
$$\begin{aligned}
(4x^3+0x^2+x-550)-(4x^3-20x^2)&=20x^2+x-550\\
(20x^2+x-550)-(20x^2-100x)&=101x-550\\
(101x-550)-(101x-505)&=-45.
\end{aligned}$$
The quotient terms are $4x^2$, $20x$ and $101$, so the blanks are $4x^2$ and $101$.
$$\frac{4x^3+x-550}{x-5}=4x^2+20x+101-\frac{45}{x-5}.$$

children.prompt:
Perform the following division and express the result in the form $\frac{P(x)}{D(x)}=Q(x)+\frac{R(x)}{D(x)}$.

$(x^3-7x+4)\div(x-3)$

answer.worked:
Insert $0x^2$. Successive leading-term divisions give $x^2$, $3x$ and $2$. Multiply each by $x-3$ and subtract:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+0x^2-7x+4)-(x^3-3x^2)&=3x^2-7x+4\\(3x^2-7x+4)-(3x^2-9x)&=2x+4\\(2x+4)-(2x-6)&=10\end{align*}$$
$$\frac{x^3-7x+4}{x-3}=x^2+3x+2+\frac{10}{x-3}$$

Insert $0x$. Successive leading-term divisions give $2x^2$, $-x$ and $1$. Multiply each by $x+1$ and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}
(2x^3+x^2+0x-11)-(2x^3+2x^2)&=-x^2-11\\
(-x^2+0x-11)-(-x^2-x)&=x-11\\
(x-11)-(x+1)&=-12.
\end{aligned}$$
$$\frac{2x^3+x^2-11}{x+1}=2x^2-x+1-\frac{12}{x+1}.$$

Insert $0x^2$ and $0x$. Successive leading-term divisions by $2x$ give $x^2$, $2x$ and $4$. Multiply each by $2x-4$ and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}
(2x^3+0x^2+0x-3)-(2x^3-4x^2)&=4x^2-3\\
(4x^2+0x-3)-(4x^2-8x)&=8x-3\\
(8x-3)-(8x-16)&=13.
\end{aligned}$$
$$\frac{2x^3-3}{2x-4}=x^2+2x+4+\frac{13}{2x-4}.$$

answer.worked:
Divide the leading terms: $x^3\div x^2=x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}(x^3-3x^2+3x-1)-x(x^2+5)&=-3x^2-2x-1.\end{aligned}$$
Next, $-3x^2\div x^2=-3$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(-3x^2-2x-1)-(-3)(x^2+5)=-2x+14.$$
The remainder has degree less than 2, so
$$\frac{x^3-3x^2+3x-1}{x^2+5}=x-3+\frac{-2x+14}{x^2+5}.$$

Divide the leading terms: $2x^3\div x^2=2x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(2x^3+4x^2-x+8)-2x(x^2+3x+2)=-2x^2-5x+8.$$
Next, $-2x^2\div x^2=-2$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(-2x^2-5x+8)-(-2)(x^2+3x+2)=x+12.$$
The remainder has degree less than 2, so
$$\frac{2x^3+4x^2-x+8}{x^2+3x+2}=2x-2+\frac{x+12}{x^2+3x+2}.$$

Divide the leading terms: $2x^4\div x^2=2x^2$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(2x^4-5x^3+2x^2+2x-5)-2x^2(x^2-2x)=-x^3+2x^2+2x-5.$$
Next, $-x^3\div x^2=-x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(-x^3+2x^2+2x-5)-(-x)(x^2-2x)=2x-5.$$
The remainder has degree less than 2, so
$$\frac{2x^4-5x^3+2x^2+2x-5}{x^2-2x}=2x^2-x+\frac{2x-5}{x^2-2x}.$$

Write the dividend as $x^5+0x^4+x^3+5x^2-6x+15$ to keep powers aligned. Divide the leading terms: $x^5\div x^2=x^3$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(x^5+x^3+5x^2-6x+15)-x^3(x^2+3)=-2x^3+5x^2-6x+15.$$
Next, $-2x^3\div x^2=-2x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(-2x^3+5x^2-6x+15)-(-2x)(x^2+3)=5x^2+15.$$
Finally, $5x^2\div x^2=5$, and
$$(5x^2+15)-5(x^2+3)=0.$$
The remainder is zero, so
$$\frac{x^5+x^3+5x^2-6x+15}{x^2+3}=x^3-2x+5.$$

answer.worked:
Multiply every term by $x+2$:
$$\color{#268cff}{\begin{aligned}x^3-x^2+x-1&=(x^2-3x+7)(x+2)-15.\end{aligned}}$$

Multiply every term by $x+1$:
$$\color{#268cff}{\begin{aligned}x^2-5x+3&=(x-6)(x+1)+9.\end{aligned}}$$

Use polynomial long division by $x+3$.
First, $2x^3\div x=2x^2$. Multiply and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}(2x^3-x^2+3x-1)-(2x^3+6x^2)&=-7x^2+3x-1.\end{aligned}$$
Next, $-7x^2\div x=-7x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}(-7x^2+3x-1)-(-7x^2-21x)&=24x-1.\end{aligned}$$
Finally, $24x\div x=24$. Multiply and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}(24x-1)-(24x+72)&=-73.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient is $2x^2-7x+24$ and the remainder is $-73$, so
$$\color{#268cff}{2x^3-x^2+3x-1=(x+3)(2x^2-7x+24)-73.}$$

content.prompt: Find $m$ and $n$ in each case.

answer.worked:
The successive quotient terms in long division are $x^2$, $0x$ and $-8$.
$$\begin{align*}(x^4-x^3-6x^2+mx+n)-x^2(x^2-x+2)&=-8x^2+mx+n\\(-8x^2+mx+n)-(-8)(x^2-x+2)&=(m-8)x+(n+16)\end{align*}$$
Exact divisibility means the remainder is zero, so
$$\begin{align*}m-8&=0\\n+16&=0\\m&=8,\qquad n=-16\end{align*}$$

The successive quotient terms in long division are $x$ and $-1$.
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+mx+n)-x(x^2+x-2)&=-x^2+(m+2)x+n\\(-x^2+(m+2)x+n)-(-1)(x^2+x-2)&=(m+3)x+(n-2)\end{align*}$$
Exact divisibility means the remainder is zero, so
$$\begin{align*}m+3&=0\\n-2&=0\\m&=-3,\qquad n=2\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Divide these polynomials and write in the form $P(x)=D(x)Q(x)+R(x)$.

answer.worked:
Long division gives quotient terms $x^2$ and $2x$:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+x^2-2x+3)-x^2(x-1)&=2x^2-2x+3\\(2x^2-2x+3)-2x(x-1)&=3\\Q(x)&=x^2+2x\\R(x)&=3\\x^3+x^2-2x+3&=(x-1)(x^2+2x)+3\end{align*}$$

Include $0x^2$ in the dividend. Long division gives quotient terms $x^2$, $-2x$ and $3$:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+0x^2-x+1)-x^2(x+2)&=-2x^2-x+1\\(-2x^2-x+1)-(-2x)(x+2)&=3x+1\\(3x+1)-3(x+2)&=-5\\Q(x)&=x^2-2x+3\\R(x)&=-5\\x^3-x+1&=(x+2)(x^2-2x+3)-5\end{align*}$$

Include $0x$ in the dividend. Long division gives quotient terms $x^2$, $2x$ and $2$:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+x^2+0x-3)-x^2(x-1)&=2x^2-3\\(2x^2+0x-3)-2x(x-1)&=2x-3\\(2x-3)-2(x-1)&=-1\\Q(x)&=x^2+2x+2\\R(x)&=-1\\x^3+x^2-3&=(x-1)(x^2+2x+2)-1\end{align*}$$

Include the missing terms with zero coefficients. Long division gives quotient terms $x^3$, $4x^2$, $15x$ and $60$:

content.prompt: If $x^4-2x^3-20x^2+mx+n$ is exactly divisible by $x^2-5x+2$, find $m$ and $n$.

answer.short: $m=41$, $n=-14$. Long division gives remainder $(m-41)x+(n+14)$; exact divisibility requires both coefficients to be zero.
answer.worked:
The successive quotient terms in long division are $x^2$, $3x$ and $-7$.
$$\begin{aligned}
(x^4-2x^3-20x^2+mx+n)-x^2(x^2-5x+2)&=3x^3-22x^2+mx+n\\
(3x^3-22x^2+mx+n)-3x(x^2-5x+2)&=-7x^2+(m-6)x+n\\
(-7x^2+(m-6)x+n)-(-7)(x^2-5x+2)&=(m-41)x+(n+14).
\end{aligned}$$
Thus
$$\begin{aligned}
x^4-2x^3-20x^2+mx+n&=(x^2-5x+2)(x^2+3x-7)+(m-41)x+(n+14).
\end{aligned}$$
Exact divisibility means the remainder is zero, so
$$\begin{aligned}
m-41&=0\\
n+14&=0\\
m&=41,\qquad n=-14.
\end{aligned}$$

content.prompt: Find the remainder in each case.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
When $P(x)$ is divided by $(x+3)(x-4)$, the remainder is $2x-5$.
Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $(x+3)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+3)(x-4)Q(x)+(2x-5)\\P(-3)&=(-3+3)(-3-4)Q(-3)+2(-3)-5\\P(-3)&=-11\end{align*}$$
By the remainder theorem, the remainder is $-11$.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
When $P(x)$ is divided by $(x^2-16)$, the remainder is $5x+1$.
Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $(x+4)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x^2-16)Q(x)+(5x+1)\\P(-4)&=\bigl((-4)^2-16\bigr)Q(-4)+5(-4)+1\\P(-4)&=-19\end{align*}$$
By the remainder theorem, the remainder is $-19$.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
When $P(x)$ is divided by $(2x-1)(x+3)$, the remainder is $4x+3$.
Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $(2x-1)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(2x-1)(x+3)Q(x)+(4x+3)\\P\left(\tfrac12\right)&=\left(2\left(\tfrac12\right)-1\right)\left(\tfrac12+3\right)Q\left(\tfrac12\right)+4\left(\tfrac12\right)+3\\P\left(\tfrac12\right)&=5\end{align*}$$
By the remainder theorem, the remainder is $5$.

content.prompt: Complete the following.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $x^n-7^n$ is divisible by $(x-7)$ for every positive integer $n$.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^n-7^n$.
$$\begin{align*}P(7)&=7^n-7^n\\P(7)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $x-7$ divides $x^n-7^n$ for every positive integer $n$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove that $x^n+2^n$ is divisible by $(x+2)$ for every odd positive integer $n$.

answer.short: $P(-2)=(-2)^n+2^n=0$ for odd $n$, so $x+2$ is a factor of $x^n+2^n$.
answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^n+2^n$.
$$\begin{align*}P(-2)&=(-2)^n+2^n\\P(-2)&=-2^n+2^n\\P(-2)&=0\end{align*}$$
Since $(-2)^n=-2^n$ for every odd positive integer $n$, the factor theorem shows that $x+2$ divides $x^n+2^n$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Prove that $x^{2n}-1$ is divisible by $(x+1)$ for every positive integer $n$.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^{2n}-1$.
$$\begin{align*}P(-1)&=(-1)^{2n}-1\\P(-1)&=1-1\\P(-1)&=0\end{align*}$$
Since $2n$ is even, $(-1)^{2n}=1$. By the factor theorem, $x+1$ divides $x^{2n}-1$ for every positive integer $n$.

content.prompt: Factorise these polynomials, and hence solve $P(x)=0$.

answer.worked:
Test integer factors of $6$.
$$P(-1)=-1-4-1+6=0.$$
Therefore $x+1$ is a factor. Use polynomial long division:
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)-x^2(x+1)&=-5x^2+x+6\\(-5x^2+x+6)-(-5x)(x+1)&=6x+6\\(6x+6)-6(x+1)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient is $x^2-5x+6$.
$$P(x)=(x+1)(x^2-5x+6)=(x+1)(x-2)(x-3).$$
Using the null factor law, $x=-1,2,3$.

Test integer factors of $30$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(1)&=1+6-1-30=-24\\P(2)&=8+24-2-30=0.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $x-2$ is a factor. Use polynomial long division:
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)-x^2(x-2)&=8x^2-x-30\\(8x^2-x-30)-8x(x-2)&=15x-30\\(15x-30)-15(x-2)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient is $x^2+8x+15$.
$$P(x)=(x-2)(x^2+8x+15)=(x-2)(x+3)(x+5).$$
Using the null factor law, $x=-5,-3,2$.

Test integer factors of $10$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(1)&=2-13+13+10=12\\P(-1)&=-2-13-13+10=-18\\P(2)&=16-52+26+10=0.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $x-2$ is a factor. Use polynomial long division:
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)-2x^2(x-2)&=-9x^2+13x+10\\(-9x^2+13x+10)-(-9x)(x-2)&=-5x+10\\(-5x+10)-(-5)(x-2)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient is $2x^2-9x-5$.
$$\begin{aligned}2x^2-9x-5&=2x^2-10x+x-5\\&=(2x+1)(x-5).\end{aligned}$$
Hence $P(x)=(x-2)(2x+1)(x-5)$. Using the null factor law, $x=-\frac12,2,5$.

Test integer factors of $5$.
$$P(1)=1+4-5=0.$$
Therefore $x-1$ is a factor. Use polynomial long division, including the zero coefficient of $x^2$:
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)-x^2(x-1)&=x^2+4x-5\\(x^2+4x-5)-x(x-1)&=5x-5\\(5x-5)-5(x-1)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Hence $P(x)=(x-1)(x^2+x+5)$. By the null factor law, $x=1$ or $x^2+x+5=0$. The quadratic has discriminant $1^2-4(1)(5)=-19<0$, so it has no real roots. Therefore $x=1$ is the only real solution.

answer.worked:
Possible integer zeroes are factors of $6$:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=2+1-14+5+6=0\\P(-1)&=2-1-14-5+6=-12\\P(2)&=32+8-56+10+6=0\\P(-2)&=32-8-56-10+6=-36\\P(3)&=162+27-126+15+6=84\\P(-3)&=162-27-126-15+6=0\end{align*}$$
Thus the integer zeroes are $1,2,-3$.
Long division by $x-1$ gives quotient $2x^3+3x^2-11x-6$ and remainder $0$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&2x^3+3x^2-11x-6\\\hline x-1&2x^4+x^3-14x^2+5x+6\\&\underline{-(2x^4-2x^3)}\\&3x^3-14x^2+5x+6\\&\underline{-(3x^3-3x^2)}\\&-11x^2+5x+6\\&\underline{-(-11x^2+11x)}\\&-6x+6\\&\underline{-(-6x+6)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Long division of the quotient by $x-2$ gives $2x^2+7x+3$ with remainder $0$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&2x^2+7x+3\\\hline x-2&2x^3+3x^2-11x-6\\&\underline{-(2x^3-4x^2)}\\&7x^2-11x-6\\&\underline{-(7x^2-14x)}\\&3x-6\\&\underline{-(3x-6)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Factorise the quadratic $2x^2+7x+3$ using PSF: Product $ac=2\times3=6$, Sum $7$, Factors $1$ and $6$.
$$\begin{align*}2x^2+7x+3&=2x^2+x+6x+3\\&=x(2x+1)+3(2x+1)\\&=(x+3)(2x+1)\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x-2)(2x^2+7x+3)\\&=(x-1)(x-2)(x+3)(2x+1).\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3-2x^2-5x+6$. Test factors of $6$: $P(1)=1-2-5+6=0$, so $x-1$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&x^2&-x&-6&\\\hline x-1&x^3&-2x^2&-5x&+6\\&x^3&-x^2&&\\\hline &&-x^2&-5x&+6\\&&-x^2&+x&\\\hline &&&-6x&+6\\&&&-6x&+6\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x^2-x-6)\\&=(x-1)(x+2)(x-3).\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=-2,\ 1,\ 3$.

Let $P(x)=x^3-6x^2+11x-6$. Test factors of $-6$: $P(1)=1-6+11-6=0$, so $x-1$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&x^2&-5x&+6&\\\hline x-1&x^3&-6x^2&+11x&-6\\&x^3&-x^2&&\\\hline &&-5x^2&+11x&-6\\&&-5x^2&+5x&\\\hline &&&6x&-6\\&&&6x&-6\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x^2-5x+6)\\&=(x-1)(x-2)(x-3).\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=1,\ 2,\ 3$.

Let $P(x)=x^3-3x^2-16x-12$. Test factors of $-12$: $P(-1)=-1-3+16-12=0$, so $x+1$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&x^2&-4x&-12&\\\hline x+1&x^3&-3x^2&-16x&-12\\&x^3&+x^2&&\\\hline &&-4x^2&-16x&-12\\&&-4x^2&-4x&\\\hline &&&-12x&-12\\&&&-12x&-12\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+1)(x^2-4x-12)\\&=(x+1)(x+2)(x-6).\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=-2,\ -1,\ 6$.

Rearrange to $2x^3-3x^2-11x+6=0$. Let $P(x)=2x^3-3x^2-11x+6$. Test factors of $6$: $P(-2)=-16-12+22+6=0$, so $x+2$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&2x^2&-7x&+3&\\\hline x+2&2x^3&-3x^2&-11x&+6\\&2x^3&+4x^2&&\\\hline &&-7x^2&-11x&+6\\&&-7x^2&-14x&\\\hline &&&3x&+6\\&&&3x&+6\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+2)(2x^2-7x+3)\\&=(x+2)(2x-1)(x-3).\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=-2,\ \frac12,\ 3$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Solve $x^3-2x^2-6x+9=0$, expressing your answers in exact form.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3-2x^2-6x+9$. Test factors of $9$:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1-2-6+9=2\\P(-1)&=-1-2+6+9=12\\P(3)&=27-18-18+9=0.\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $x-3$ is a factor. Divide by $x-3$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2+x-3\\\hline x-3&x^3-2x^2-6x+9\\&\underline{-(x^3-3x^2)}\\&x^2-6x+9\\&\underline{-(x^2-3x)}\\&-3x+9\\&\underline{-(-3x+9)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Thus
$$(x-3)(x^2+x-3)=0.$$
By the null factor law, $x=3$ or $x^2+x-3=0$. For the quadratic:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{1^2-4(1)(-3)}}{2}\\&=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{13}}{2}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=3,\ \dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt{13}}{2}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Solve $x^3-x^2-11x+3=0$, expressing your answers in exact form.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3-x^2-11x+3$. Test factors of $3$:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1-1-11+3=-8\\P(-1)&=-1-1+11+3=12\\P(3)&=27-9-33+3=-12\\P(-3)&=-27-9+33+3=0.\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $x+3$ is a factor. Divide by $x+3$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2-4x+1\\\hline x+3&x^3-x^2-11x+3\\&\underline{-(x^3+3x^2)}\\&-4x^2-11x+3\\&\underline{-(-4x^2-12x)}\\&x+3\\&\underline{-(x+3)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Thus
$$(x+3)(x^2-4x+1)=0.$$
By the null factor law, $x=-3$ or $x^2-4x+1=0$. For the quadratic:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-(-4)\pm\sqrt{(-4)^2-4(1)(1)}}{2}\\&=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{12}}{2}\\&=2\pm\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=-3,\ 2\pm\sqrt3$.

content.prompt: Solve $x^3-3x^2-2x+2=0$, expressing your answers in exact form.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3-3x^2-2x+2$. Test factors of $2$:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1-3-2+2=-2\\P(-1)&=-1-3+2+2=0.\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $x+1$ is a factor. Divide by $x+1$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2-4x+2\\\hline x+1&x^3-3x^2-2x+2\\&\underline{-(x^3+x^2)}\\&-4x^2-2x+2\\&\underline{-(-4x^2-4x)}\\&2x+2\\&\underline{-(2x+2)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Thus
$$(x+1)(x^2-4x+2)=0.$$
By the null factor law, $x=-1$ or $x^2-4x+2=0$. For the quadratic:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-(-4)\pm\sqrt{(-4)^2-4(1)(2)}}{2}\\&=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{8}}{2}\\&=2\pm\sqrt2.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=-1,\ 2\pm\sqrt2$.

content.prompt: Use trial and error to find as many integer zeroes of $P(x)$ as possible, then use long division to find the other factors.

answer.short:
Integer zeroes: $-1,1,3$.
$P(x)=(x-1)(x+1)(x-3)(2x+1)$; the remaining zero is $-\frac{1}{2}$.
answer.worked:
Test the possible integer zeroes $\pm1,\pm3$:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=2-5-5+5+3=0\\P(-1)&=2+5-5-5+3=0\\P(3)&=162-135-45+15+3=0\\P(-3)&=162+135-45-15+3=240\end{align*}$$
Thus the integer zeroes are $1,-1,3$.
Long division by $x-1$ gives quotient $2x^3-3x^2-8x-3$ and remainder $0$. The successive subtraction results are
$$\begin{align*}P(x)-2x^3(x-1)&=-3x^3-5x^2+5x+3\\{}-(-3x^2)(x-1)&=-8x^2+5x+3\\{}-(-8x)(x-1)&=-3x+3\\{}-(-3)(x-1)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Long division of the quotient by $x+1$ gives $2x^2-5x-3$ with remainder $0$:
$$\begin{align*}(2x^3-3x^2-8x-3)-2x^2(x+1)&=-5x^2-8x-3\\{}-(-5x)(x+1)&=-3x-3\\{}-(-3)(x+1)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Factorise the quadratic:
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x+1)(2x^2-5x-3)\\&=(x-1)(x+1)(x-3)(2x+1).\end{align*}$$
The remaining zero is $-\frac12$.

answer.short:
Integer zeroes: $-1,2$.
$P(x)=(2x-5)(3x-2)(x+1)(x-2)$; the remaining zeroes are $\frac{5}{2},\frac{2}{3}$.

content.prompt: Explain why $(x-2)(x^2-3x+3)=0$ has only one real solution.

answer.short: $\Delta=(-3)^2-4(1)(3)=-3<0$, so the quadratic has no real roots. The only real solution is $x=2$.
answer.worked: For $x^2-3x+3$, $$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-3)^2-4(1)(3)\\\Delta&=9-12\\\Delta&=-3<0\end{align*}$$ Thus $x^2-3x+3=0$ has no real solutions. By the null factor law, the only real solution comes from $x-2=0$, giving $x=2$.

answer.worked:
The square base has side length $x$ cm and the height is $(x+2)$ cm.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the volume is to be $45\text{ cm}^3$, write a polynomial equation modelling this scenario.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the dimensions that will give this volume.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3+2x^2-45$. Test factors of $45$:
$$P(3)=27+18-45=0.$$
Therefore $x-3$ is a factor. Long division gives
$$\begin{array}{r|rrrr}&x^2&+5x&+15&\\\hline x-3&x^3&+2x^2&+0x&-45\\&x^3&-3x^2&&\\\hline &&5x^2&+0x&-45\\&&5x^2&-15x&\\\hline &&&15x&-45\\&&&15x&-45\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
Thus
$$(x-3)(x^2+5x+15)=0.$$
The quadratic has discriminant $5^2-4(1)(15)=-35<0$, so its roots are not real. Hence $x=3$ cm and the height is $x+2=5$ cm. The box dimensions are $3\text{ cm}\times3\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}$.

content.prompt: A box has a square base of side length $x$ cm and a height that is 3 cm less than the length of the base. The volume of the box is $50\text{ cm}^3$. Write a polynomial equation modelling this scenario and hence find the dimensions of the box.

answer.short: $x^3-3x^2-50=0$; the box is $5\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
The base has side length $x$ cm and the height is $(x-3)$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}x^2(x-3)&=50\\x^3-3x^2&=50\\x^3-3x^2-50&=0\end{align*}$$
Let $P(x)=x^3-3x^2-50$. Test factors of $50$:
$$P(5)=125-75-50=0.$$
Therefore $x-5$ is a factor. Long division, with the missing $x$ term shown as $0x$, gives
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2+2x+10\\\hline x-5&x^3-3x^2+0x-50\\&\underline{-(x^3-5x^2)}\\&2x^2+0x-50\\&\underline{-(2x^2-10x)}\\&10x-50\\&\underline{-(10x-50)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Hence
$$(x-5)(x^2+2x+10)=0.$$
The quadratic has discriminant $2^2-4(1)(10)=-36<0$, so its roots are not real. Hence $x=5$ cm and the height is $x-3=2$ cm. The box dimensions are $5\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.

content.prompt: Show that $x^3+x^2+3x-5=0$ has exactly one real solution.

answer.short: $(x-1)(x^2+2x+5)=0$. The quadratic has $\Delta=-16<0$, so $x=1$ is the only real solution.
answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3+x^2+3x-5$. Test factors of $-5$:
$$P(1)=1+1+3-5=0.$$
By the factor theorem, $x-1$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&x^2&+2x&+5&\\\hline x-1&x^3&+x^2&+3x&-5\\&x^3&-x^2&&\\\hline &&2x^2&+3x&-5\\&&2x^2&-2x&\\\hline &&&5x&-5\\&&&5x&-5\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$(x-1)(x^2+2x+5)=0.$$
For $x^2+2x+5$,
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=2^2-4(1)(5)\\&=-16<0.\end{align*}$$
The quadratic has no real zeros. By the null factor law, the only real solution comes from $x-1=0$, so $x=1$.

content.prompt: A rectangular box has width $x$ cm, a length that is 2 cm more than its width and a height that is 3 cm less than its width. The volume of the box is $70\text{ cm}^3$. Write a polynomial equation modelling this scenario and hence find the dimensions of the box.

answer.short: $x^3-x^2-6x-70=0$; the box is $7\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
The width is $x$ cm, the length is $(x+2)$ cm and the height is $(x-3)$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+2)(x-3)&=70\\x(x^2-x-6)&=70\\x^3-x^2-6x-70&=0\end{align*}$$
Let $P(x)=x^3-x^2-6x-70$. Test factors of $70$:
$$P(5)=125-25-30-70=0.$$
Therefore $x-5$ is a factor. Long division gives
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2+4x+14\\\hline x-5&x^3-x^2-6x-70\\&\underline{-(x^3-5x^2)}\\&4x^2-6x-70\\&\underline{-(4x^2-20x)}\\&14x-70\\&\underline{-(14x-70)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Hence
$$(x-5)(x^2+4x+14)=0.$$
The quadratic has discriminant $4^2-4(1)(14)=-40<0$, so its roots are not real. Hence $x=5$ cm, the length is $x+2=7$ cm and the height is $x-3=2$ cm. The box dimensions are $7\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.

answer.worked:

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the side length of the square that should be cut from each corner if the volume is to be $48\text{ cm}^3$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x(8-2x)(10-2x)&=48\\4x^3-36x^2+80x-48&=0\\x^3-9x^2+20x-12&=0.\end{align*}$$
Let $P(x)=x^3-9x^2+20x-12$. Test factors of $12$:
$$P(1)=1-9+20-12=0.$$
Therefore $x-1$ is a factor. Long division gives
$$\begin{array}{r|rrrr}&x^2&-8x&+12&\\\hline x-1&x^3&-9x^2&+20x&-12\\&x^3&-x^2&&\\\hline &&-8x^2&+20x&-12\\&&-8x^2&+8x&\\\hline &&&12x&-12\\&&&12x&-12\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)(x^2-8x+12)&=0\\(x-1)(x-2)(x-6)&=0.\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=1,2,6$. A box requires $0<x<4$, so reject $x=6$. The cut squares must have side length $1$ cm or $2$ cm.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence state the dimensions of the rectangular box with this volume.

answer.short: $8\text{ cm}\times6\text{ cm}\times1\text{ cm}$ or $6\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
For $x=1$, the base dimensions are $10-2(1)=8$ cm and $8-2(1)=6$ cm, and the height is $1$ cm.
For $x=2$, the base dimensions are $10-2(2)=6$ cm and $8-2(2)=4$ cm, and the height is $2$ cm.
Thus the dimensions are $8\text{ cm}\times6\text{ cm}\times1\text{ cm}$ or $6\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$; both volumes are $48\text{ cm}^3$.

spec.mathematics: The cube's side elevation is a unit square. The ladder joins (0,H) to (D,0), where H≈9.93799368936 and D≈1.11188193176, with H²+D²=100 and 1/H+1/D=1, so it passes through (1,1).

answer.short: Similar triangles give $y=\frac1x$. Substituting into $(x+1)^2+(y+1)^2=100$ gives $x^4+2x^3-98x^2+2x+1=0$.
answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2+(1+y)^2&=10^2.\end{align*}$$
Using similar triangles:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{y}{1}&=\frac{1}{x}\\y&=\frac{1}{x}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute, expand and multiply every term by $x^2$:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2+\left(1+\frac1x\right)^2&=100\\x^2+2x+2+\frac2x+\frac1{x^2}&=100\\x^4+2x^3+2x^2+2x+1&=100x^2\\x^4+2x^3-98x^2+2x+1&=0.\end{align*}$$

Find the value of $a$.

answer.worked:
Since $(2x+1)$ is a factor, $P\left(-\frac12\right)=0$.
$$\begin{align*}2\left(-\tfrac12\right)^3+a\left(-\tfrac12\right)^2-\tfrac12+2&=0\\-\tfrac14+\tfrac a4+\tfrac32&=0\\a+5&=0\\a&=-5\end{align*}$$

Let $P(x)=x^2-2ax+a^4$ where $a$ is a non-zero real number.
When $P(x)$ is divided by $x+b$, the remainder is $1$.
The polynomial $Q(x)=bx^2+x+1$ has a factor of $(ax-1)$.

answer.worked:
Since $P(x)$ divided by $x+b$ has remainder $1$, $P(-b)=1$.
$$\begin{align*}
P(-b) &= 1 \\
b^2+2ab+a^4 &= 1
\end{align*}$$
Since $Q(x)$ has a factor of $(ax-1)$, $x=\frac{1}{a}$ is a root of $Q(x)$.
$$\begin{align*}
Q\left(\frac{1}{a}\right) &= 0 \\
b\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^2+\frac{1}{a}+1 &= 0 \\
\frac{b}{a^2}+\frac{1}{a}+1 &= 0 \\
b+a+a^2 &= 0 \\
b &= -a^2-a
\end{align*}$$
Substitute into $b^2+2ab+a^4=1$:
$$\begin{align*}
(-a^2-a)^2+2a(-a^2-a)+a^4 &= 1 \\
a^4+2a^3+a^2-2a^3-2a^2+a^4 &= 1 \\
2a^4-a^2-1 &= 0 \\
(2a^2+1)(a^2-1) &= 0
\end{align*}$$
Since $a$ is real, $a^2=1$, so $a=\pm 1$.
$$\begin{align*}
a=1 &\implies b=-1^2-1=-2 \\
a=-1 &\implies b=-(-1)^2-(-1)=0
\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $b=-2$ or $b=0$.

content.prompt: Factorise $x^4-x^3-5x^2+12$.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^4-x^3-5x^2+12$. Test an integer factor of $12$:
$$\begin{aligned}P(2)&=16-8-20+12\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$
So $x-2$ is a factor. Polynomial long division gives
$$\begin{array}{r|rrrr} &x^3&+x^2&-3x&-6\\\hline x-2&x^4&-x^3&-5x^2&+0x+12\\ &x^4&-2x^3&&\\\hline &&x^3&-5x^2&+0x+12\\ &&x^3&-2x^2&\\\hline &&&-3x^2&+0x+12\\ &&&-3x^2&+6x\\\hline &&&&-6x+12\\ &&&&-6x+12\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
For $Q(x)=x^3+x^2-3x-6$,
$$\begin{aligned}Q(2)&=8+4-6-6\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Thus $x-2$ is also a factor of $Q(x)$. Dividing again:
$$\begin{array}{r|rrr} &x^2&+3x&+3\\\hline x-2&x^3&+x^2&-3x-6\\ &x^3&-2x^2&\\\hline &&3x^2&-3x-6\\ &&3x^2&-6x\\\hline &&&3x-6\\ &&&3x-6\\\hline &&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)&=(x-2)(x^3+x^2-3x-6)\\&=(x-2)^2(x^2+3x+3).\end{aligned}$$

content.prompt: Divide these polynomials and express in the form $\frac{P(x)}{D(x)}=Q(x)+\frac{R(x)}{D(x)}$.

answer.worked:
Successive quotient terms:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{-2x^3}{x}&=-2x^2\\\frac{6x^2}{x}&=6x\\\frac{-29x}{x}&=-29\end{align*}$$
Subtract each divisor multiple:
$$\begin{align*}(-2x^3-2x^2-5x+7)-(-2x^3-8x^2)&=6x^2-5x+7\\(6x^2-5x+7)-(6x^2+24x)&=-29x+7\\(-29x+7)-(-29x-116)&=123\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\frac{-2x^3-2x^2-5x+7}{x+4}=-2x^2+6x-29+\frac{123}{x+4}.$$

Include the missing $x^2$ term as $0x^2$. Successive quotient terms:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x^3}{x}&=x^2\\\frac{2x^2}{x}&=2x\\\frac{-x}{x}&=-1\end{align*}$$
Subtract each divisor multiple:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+0x^2-5x+3)-(x^3-2x^2)&=2x^2-5x+3\\(2x^2-5x+3)-(2x^2-4x)&=-x+3\\(-x+3)-(-x+2)&=1\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\frac{x^3-5x+3}{x-2}=x^2+2x-1+\frac{1}{x-2}.$$

Include the missing $x^2$ term as $0x^2$. Successive quotient terms:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x^3}{x}&=x^2\\\frac{-x^2}{x}&=-x\\\frac{-2x}{x}&=-2\end{align*}$$
Subtract each divisor multiple:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+0x^2-3x-2)-(x^3+x^2)&=-x^2-3x-2\\(-x^2-3x-2)-(-x^2-x)&=-2x-2\\(-2x-2)-(-2x-2)&=0\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\frac{x^3-3x-2}{x+1}=x^2-x-2.$$

An odd cubic has the form $P(x)=ax^3+bx$, since $P(-x)=-P(x)$.

Bridge for Q7 to Q9.

1) The remainder when $P(x)=x^2+5x-3$ is divided by $(x-c)$ is $11$.
a) By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is $P(c)=$ [[ ]]
b) Write $P(c)=11$ and rearrange to zero: [[ ]] $=0$
c) PSF: Product [[ ]]  Sum [[ ]]  Factors [[ ]] and [[ ]]
d) Solve for $c$: [[ ]]
e) State the divisors $(x-c)$: [[ ]]

2) Reset: Find the divisors of $x^2-3x-9$ that leave a remainder of $1$.
a) Let the divisor be $(x-c)$. Write $P(c)=1$ and rearrange to zero: [[ ]] $=0$
b) PSF: Product [[ ]]  Sum [[ ]]  Factors [[ ]] and [[ ]]
c) Solve for $c$: [[ ]]
d) State the divisors: [[ ]]

Answers:
1a) $c^2+5c-3$.
1b) $c^2+5c-3=11$, so $c^2+5c-14=0$.
1c) PSF: Product $-14$; Sum $5$; Factors $7$ and $-2$. $(c+7)(c-2)=0$.
1d) $c=-7$ or $c=2$.
1e) $x+7$ or $x-2$.
2a) $c^2-3c-9=1$, so $c^2-3c-10=0$.
2b) PSF: Product $-10$; Sum $-3$; Factors $-5$ and $2$. $(c-5)(c+2)=0$.
2c) $c=5$ or $c=-2$.
2d) $x-5$ or $x+2$.

Bridge for Q24(a). Use the ladder diagram. The wall height reached is $x+1$ m and the distance along the ground is $y+1$ m.

i) The cube has edge $1$ m. The length of wall above the cube's top edge is [[ ]] m. The length of ground beyond the cube is [[ ]] m.

ii) The triangle above the cube has legs $1$ m (horizontal) and $x$ m (vertical). The triangle beside the cube has legs $y$ m (horizontal) and $1$ m (vertical). Both lie along the ladder, so they are similar. Complete: $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{1}{[[ ]]}$, so $y=$ [[ ]]

iii) The ladder is the hypotenuse of the large right-angled triangle. Write Pythagoras' theorem in terms of $x$ and $y$: $(x+1)^2+(y+1)^2=$ [[ ]]

iv) To get an equation in $x$ only, replace $y$ in part iii by [[ ]]

Answers:
i) $x$ and $y$, because $(x+1)-1=x$ and $(y+1)-1=y$.
ii) $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{1}{y}$, so $xy=1$ and $y=\frac{1}{x}$.
iii) $100$, because the ladder is $10$ m and $10^2=100$. $(x+1)^2+(y+1)^2=100$.
iv) $\frac{1}{x}$.

Worked example: Prove that $x^n-2^n$ is divisible by $(x-2)$ for every positive integer $n$.
Let $P(x)=x^n-2^n$.
$$\begin{align*}P(2)&=2^n-2^n\\P(2)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $x-2$ divides $x^n-2^n$ for every positive integer $n$.

c) Prove that $x^{2n}-1$ is divisible by $(x+1)$ for every positive integer $n$.

[Pedagogy audit v2 · Applied automatically · New teaching] Question 12 and the backfill group need students to divide with unknown $m$ and $n$ and set both remainder coefficients to zero, but no teaching shows it. Add a worked example.
Worked example: If $x^4+2x^3-7x^2+mx+n$ is exactly divisible by $x^2+x-3$, find $m$ and $n$.
The successive quotient terms in long division are $x^2$, $x$ and $-5$.
$$\begin{align*}(x^4+2x^3-7x^2+mx+n)-x^2(x^2+x-3)&=x^3-4x^2+mx+n\\(x^3-4x^2+mx+n)-x(x^2+x-3)&=-5x^2+(m+3)x+n\\(-5x^2+(m+3)x+n)-(-5)(x^2+x-3)&=(m+8)x+(n-15)\end{align*}$$
Thus
$$x^4+2x^3-7x^2+mx+n=(x^2+x-3)(x^2+x-5)+(m+8)x+(n-15).$$
Exact divisibility means the remainder is zero, so
$$\begin{align*}m+8&=0\\n-15&=0\\m&=-8,\qquad n=15\end{align*}$$
Guided practice:
Proposed question: Find $m$ and $n$ in each case.
a) $x^4-x^3-6x^2+mx+n$ is exactly divisible by $x^2-x+2$.
b) $x^3+mx+n$ is exactly divisible by $x^2+x-2$.
Answers: a) $m=8$, $n=-16$.; b) $m=-3$, $n=2$.

entries.description:
Syllabus Content
MA5-POL-P-01 defines, operates with and graphs polynomials and applies the factor and remainder theorems to solve problems
Recognise a polynomial expression a_n x^n + a_{n−1}x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_2x^2 + a_1x + a_0 where n = 0, 1, 2 … and a_0, a_1, a_2, …, a_n are real numbers
Describe polynomials using terms such as degree, leading term, coefficient and leading coefficient, constant term, monic and non-monic
Define a monic polynomial as having a leading coefficient of one
Apply the notation P(x) for polynomials and P(c) to indicate the value of P(x) for x = c
Identify the dividend, divisor, quotient and remainder in numerical division
Divide a polynomial by a linear polynomial to find the quotient and remainder
Express a polynomial in the form P(x) = D(x)Q(x) + R(x), where D(x) is the divisor, Q(x) is the quotient and R(x) is the remainder

entries.sourceLabel: Apply the factor and remainder theorems to solve problems
entries.description: Apply the factor and remainder theorems to solve problems
Verify the remainder theorem and use it to find factors of polynomials and solve related problems
Develop and apply the factor theorem to factorise particular polynomials completely and solve related problems
Apply the factor theorem and division to find the zeroes of a polynomial P(x) and solve P(x) = 0 (degree ≤ 4)
State the maximum number of zeroes a polynomial of degree n can have

entries.description:
A polynomial in factored form is P(x) = k(x − a)(x − b)(x − c)(x − d) …
The x-intercepts are at x = a, b, c, d …
1. Determine curve behaviour at x → ∞ (identify leading coefficient).
• If leading coefficient is positive, then x → ∞, y → ∞.
• If leading coefficient is negative, then x → ∞, y → −∞.
2. Determine the y-intercept by letting x = 0 (multiply constant terms in each factor).
3. Determine the x-intercepts by letting y = 0 (use null-factor law).

entries.description:
We will apply this idea to polynomials:
Last lesson we used polynomial division to show that, given a dividend P(x), divisor D(x), quotient Q(x), and remainder R(x):
P(x)/D(x) = Q(x) + R(x)/D(x).
We multiply every term by D(x) to derive the quotient-remainder form of a polynomial:
P(x) = Q(x)D(x) + R(x).
Two important facts:
• The degree of the remainder is always less than the divisor: deg R(x) < deg D(x).
• When R(x) = 0, then Q(x) and D(x) are factors of P(x): P(x) = Q(x) × D(x).

entries.description:
Integer Root Theorem
If all coefficients of P(x) are integers, then all integer roots (if they exist) are factors of the constant term.
P(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 − 5x − 6 = (x + 1)(x − 2)(x + 3),
the integer roots are factors of −6
P(x) = x^3 + x^2 + x + 6 = (x + 2)(x^2 − x + 3),
the integer root is a factor of 6
